title: Agents reported thousands of bugs, how many were real? - Ian Butler and Nick Gregory
talk_summary: Bismouth benchmarked agents on 100 real, triaged bugs across 84 repos (SM-100) and found basic agent loops produce ~97% false positives, most popular agents score ~7%, and even the best PR-review agent finds only ~27% of bugs. Their core diagnosis: agents reason narrowly, don't inventory files holistically, and per-run bug sets vary, so single-pass review is unreliable.

takeaways.technique: Tight scoping to a subsystem instead of whole-repo scans
takeaways.what_they_do: They partition repos into interrelated-file subsystems and feed only the relevant subsystem's file list to the agent, avoiding both whole-repo search and hinting at the bug.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're still scoping it down so it doesn't have to look through everything
takeaways.numbers: Basic loop: 5-6 bugs found but 97% false positive rate

takeaways.technique: Multi-run sampling with union/dedup instead of trusting one pass
takeaways.what_they_do: They observed that per-run bug counts stay constant but the specific bugs change, so any single run misses bugs; they imply repeated runs over the same context are needed to surface more.
takeaways.evidence_quote: on a perr run basis, the total number of bugs remains roughly consistent, but the bugs themselves change
takeaways.numbers: 0-day example: ~100 runs over same context to find it

takeaways.technique: Objective-bug benchmark with triaged ground truth and FP measurement
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a 100-bug benchmark of validated, already-fixed bugs in public repos, annotated with severity/domain-knowledge/difficulty, and manually measured false positives alongside true positives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we painstakingly gathered 100 bugs that we triaged, validated, and classified in over 84 public repositories
takeaways.numbers: 100 bugs, 84 repos; best PR-review agent 27% recall; top popular agent 7%

takeaways.technique: Route by task type, not one model for all
takeaways.what_they_do: They show large per-task and per-model variance: Codex strong on PR review (27%), Claude Code 16%, open models near 1-2% true positive on bug detection, so model choice should depend on the task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: codeex was quite strong uh with 20 uh 27% of the needle in haststack found
takeaways.numbers: Codex 27%, Bismouth 17%, Claude Code 16% on PR review; R1 1% and Llama Maverick 2% TPR

takeaways.technique: Force broad-then-deep reasoning, not narrow single-pass
takeaways.what_they_do: They diagnose that thinking models explore too few avenues and don't go deep enough, and prescribe broader thinking chains plus deeper exploration along selected chains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: broader thinking chains and deeper thinking along selected chains is going to be required to actually find bugs

takeaways.technique: Cap and rank findings to avoid report floods
takeaways.what_they_do: They note agents emitting hundreds to thousands of low-precision reports are unusable because no engineer will sift them; tighter-scoped agents produced far fewer, higher-precision items.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent gave us an astounding 70 reports and nobody's going to actually sift through that many
